Key Takeaways

  • Section 22A of the Registration Act lists properties whose sale/registration is prohibited or restricted.
  • This covers government land, endowment and wakf land, assigned lands, and lands under specific disputes.
  • If a property is on the 22A list, the Sub-Registrar will refuse to register your sale — after you've paid.
  • We check the property against the prohibited-property database and revenue records.
  • Essential for plots, layouts and agricultural land in and around Hyderabad.

A 22A check tells you whether a property can legally be bought and registered at all. Certain categories of land — government, endowment, wakf, assigned and disputed — are placed on a prohibited list and cannot be transferred to a private buyer.

JaaGa verifies the Section 22A status of any Hyderabad or Telangana property so you never pay for land the registrar will later refuse to register.

When You Need a 22A Check

Before buying any plot, layout or agricultural parcel — especially attractively priced land on the city outskirts.

Whenever land was originally assigned by the government, or sits near lakes, temples, wakf property or government institutions.

How We Verify 22A Status

  1. 1

    Identify the Parcel

    We locate the exact survey number and village/mandal for the property.

  2. 2

    Prohibited-List Search

    We check the parcel against the Section 22A prohibited-property database and revenue classifications.

  3. 3

    Cross-Check Category

    We confirm whether the land is patta, assigned, endowment, wakf or government-classified.

  4. 4

    Clear Report

    You receive a report stating whether the property is prohibited, restricted or free to register.

Documents Required

  • Survey number and sub-division
  • Village / mandal / district
  • Current owner name
  • Any existing pattadhar passbook or deed

Common Problems We Solve

Assigned land sold as patta

Assigned lands are frequently sold illegally. We confirm the land classification, not just the seller's word.

Partial survey-number prohibition

Sometimes only part of a survey number is prohibited. We check the exact sub-division.

Recently added entries

The prohibited list is updated over time. We check the current status, not an old copy.

Why Prohibited Land Report (22A) Matters

Buyers lose money every year on 22A land — the deal looks great, the advance is paid, and only at the registration counter does the Sub-Registrar reveal the property is prohibited. A 22A report catches this before, not after.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Section 22A?

A provision of the Registration Act under which the government notifies categories of land — government, endowment, wakf, assigned, disputed — whose registration is prohibited or restricted.

What happens if I buy 22A land?

The Sub-Registrar will refuse to register the sale, so you cannot get legal ownership, and recovering your money from the seller can be very difficult.

Can 22A status change?

Yes. Properties are added to and occasionally removed from the list, so a current check matters.

Does this apply to flats?

It applies primarily to land. For flats, the underlying land's 22A status still matters and we check it.

Can you check remotely?

Yes. Send the survey number and village details and we verify without a site visit.
